_meta.source: Schematic grain corridors drawn through named ports and chokepoints; waypoints are real places, the line between them is a straight schematic segment, not a vessel track. Chokepoint transits (the diamonds on the map) are the measured quantity and come from IMF PortWatch via data/portwatch.json.
_meta.notes: Hand-authored 2026-09-17 by the owner's assistant from public route descriptions: USDA Grain Transportation Report (US Gulf export corridor, Mississippi barge system), Bolsa de Comercio de Rosario (Parana-Paraguay waterway), World Weather Attribution and Brazilian port reports (Amazon northern arc), UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport (Suez, Bab el-Mandeb, Malacca, Turkish Straits routes), CCNR market observation (Rhine). Every coordinate and route leg was checked independently on 2026-09-17 (44 waypoints within 0.3 degrees of the named place; four legs re-routed around land: Aceh, the Taiwan Strait, southern Sinai, the Horn of Africa). Each corridor inherits its ENSO phase tag from the lane it serves in data/enso_lanes.json; the phase is published evidence, not a fit. Review yearly or when a lane is added.

corridors.name: US Gulf grain to East Asia through Panama
waypoints: New Orleans, Lower Mississippi export elevators
Colon, Atlantic entrance of the Panama Canal
Balboa, Pacific exit of the Panama Canal
corridors.basis: USDA Grain Transportation Report: the US Gulf ships most US corn and soybean exports, and the Panama Canal is the shortest route from the Gulf to East Asian buyers; when the canal cuts daily slots, cargoes reroute via the Cape of Good Hope or the Suez Canal or move to Pacific Northwest ports. The last leg crosses the dateline westward.

corridors.name: Amazon barge corridor, Porto Velho to the Atlantic
corridors.basis: Brazil's northern arc moves Mato Grosso soy and corn by barge down the Madeira and Tapajos to Amazon ports. In September and October 2023 the Madeira fell so low that Porto Velho suspended loading for the first time and barge traffic halted for weeks; World Weather Attribution found climate warming the main driver of that drought, with El Nino contributing about equally to the rainfall deficit.
sources: Porto Velho and ANTAQ port reports, 2023

corridors.name: Parana-Paraguay waterway to the Gran Rosario terminals
waypoints: Buenos Aires, Rio de la Plata
corridors.basis: The Gran Rosario terminals hold about four fifths of Argentina's oilseed crushing capacity and ship more than nine tenths of its soybean and soy-product exports; the Parana's low-water spell ran from 2019 to 2023, with the lowest level since 1944 in 2021 during La Nina, cutting draught and forcing lighter loads (Bolsa de Comercio de Rosario).
sources: Argentine Naval Prefecture draught notices (via lane evidence)

corridors.name: Mississippi River barge corridor, St. Louis to the Gulf
corridors.basis: About 46 percent of US grain exports reach port by barge, most of it down the Mississippi to the Gulf; low water in the La Nina autumn of 2022 cut barge drafts and tow sizes and lifted freight rates (USDA Grain Transportation Report, USGS gauges).

corridors.name: Indian Ocean to China through the Strait of Malacca
waypoints: off Diamond Point, northwest entrance of the Strait
corridors.basis: The Strait carries Middle East and African cargoes and grain that came through Suez toward China and Southeast Asia. The El Nino tag is the lane's published evidence in data/enso_lanes.json; this corridor file adds no claim of its own about the Strait.

corridors.name: Rhine, Rotterdam to Basel
corridors.basis: Europe's main inland grain and feed artery; the Kaub gauge sets how much a barge can load. No credible ENSO link is published for Rhine water levels, so the corridor is drawn grey.

corridors.name: Black Sea grain through the Turkish Straits to Egypt
corridors.basis: Ukrainian and Russian wheat reaches Egypt, one of the two largest wheat importers in the world alongside Indonesia, through the Straits; the corridor is drawn because the Straits are a measured chokepoint, with no published ENSO link.

corridors.name: Mediterranean to the Red Sea through the Suez Canal
waypoints: Strait of Gubal, Gulf of Suez exit
corridors.basis: Black Sea and European grain bound for East Africa and Asia transit Suez; the 2024 Red Sea attacks moved much traffic to the Cape route. No published ENSO link; drawn grey.

corridors.name: Red Sea to the Indian Ocean through Bab el-Mandeb
corridors.basis: Grain for Ethiopia, Djibouti, Kenya and the Horn passes the strait; the corridor rounds the Horn by sea to Mombasa. It is drawn as a chokepoint corridor, with no published ENSO link to the strait itself.
